sources.title: RMSIDE strict parser and command table
RMSIDE setup context and its run-setting labels
Packaged support bundles: the built-in names and values of each shipped profile
Community random map scripting documentation, chiefly Zetnus' Definitive Random Map Scripting Guide; research evidence only, no text reproduced

terms.name: <PLAYER_SETUP>
terms.summary: Starts the section that decides how players are placed on the map.
details: It holds `random_placement`, `grouped_by_team`, `direct_placement`, `nomad_resources`, and `force_nomad_treaty`; those commands have no effect in any other section.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: <LAND_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that lays the base terrain and grows the lands: one for each player and any number of neutral ones.
details: Outside blocks it takes `base_terrain` and `base_layer`; `create_player_lands` and `create_land` open the blocks that describe each land. The lands paint their starting squares in script order and then grow together, one tile per land at a time, until each reaches its size.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: <ELEVATION_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that raises hills with `create_elevation`.
details: Elevation runs after the lands and before cliffs and terrains, so its `base_terrain` filters see the terrain the lands left. Whether or not the section exists, the heights are smoothed afterwards so that neighbouring tiles differ by at most one level.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: <CLIFF_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that draws cliffs; its commands set their number, length, shape, and spacing.
details: Cliffs are only made when the section holds at least one command: a header alone makes none, while any one setting, even at its default value, is enough. The commands are read outside blocks only; anything inside braces is ignored. Cliffs keep clear of every land origin and of water.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

evidence.note: An empty section makes no cliffs in our engine; a community guide says a bare header makes default cliffs.

terms.name: <TERRAIN_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that paints terrains in clumps with `create_terrain`.
details: Each `create_terrain` paints in script order on top of what the lands, cliffs, and earlier terrains left, so a later terrain can use an earlier one as its `base_terrain`.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: <CONNECTION_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that paints paths between lands, for example roads or shallows across water.
details: Each `create_connect_…` command chooses which lands to join; its block sets what paths cost to cross each terrain and what they paint. After the connections, land next to water gets its shore terrain.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: <OBJECTS_GENERATION>
terms.summary: Starts the section that places objects: units, buildings, resources, and decorations.
details: Objects are placed in script order, and each placement takes up space that later commands cannot use. `create_object` places one kind of object, `create_object_group` names a weighted set of kinds, and `create_actor_area` marks an area for later rules.

Sections may appear in any order and more than once; a header only decides where the commands after it belong. The game always generates player setup, lands, elevation, cliffs, terrains, connections, and objects in that order, whatever the order in the script.

terms.name: #define
terms.summary: Defines a label, so that `if` with that label holds.
details: Used as a number the label stands for 0; `if` only asks whether it is defined. The first definition of a name wins: a later `#define` or `#const` of the same name is ignored, and so is a name the game already defines. Inside a branch that does not run, nothing is defined.

terms.name: #undefine
terms.summary: Accepted, but the name stays defined afterwards: it does not turn a label off.
details: Do not rely on it to switch a label off later in the script; choose labels with `if` and `else` instead.

evidence.note: Our strict parser treats it as inert (parser test); community documentation says it removes the name. Not checked against the game.

terms.name: #const
terms.summary: Defines a named number.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A number, a defined name, `rnd(min,max)`, or a calculation in parentheses such as `(WIDTH * 2 + 1)`.

details: The value is worked out once, where the constant is defined; every later use reads that same number, so a constant holding `rnd(…)` keeps one result for the whole script. The first definition of a name wins, including the names the game defines before the script runs.

In a calculation, `(` touches the first value and `)` the last, with spaces around each of `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, and `%`. It is worked out strictly from left to right, without operator precedence: `(2 + 3 * 4)` is 20. Dividing by zero gives 0, and `%` works on whole numbers.
Inside a branch that does not run, the value is still worked out (and its random numbers drawn), but the name is not defined. Without a value nothing is defined.

terms.name: #include
terms.summary: Runs another script file at this point, as if its text were written here.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: A relative path, with or without quotes.

details: The file is looked up next to the script first, then in the game folders. Paths use `/` or `\`, and may not contain `..` or a drive. Each file runs at most once: a repeated or circular include is skipped. A missing file is skipped with a warning, as in the game. A quoted path may contain spaces. Includes inside a branch that does not run, or inside a comment, are skipped.
The game’s own include files open only while a game folder is linked.

terms.name: #include_drs
terms.summary: Runs a file from the game’s data at this point; it works like `#include`.
details: The game reads the definitions of `random_map.def` before every script, so including it again changes nothing.

terms.name: #includeXS
terms.summary: Attaches an XS script file to the map; its code runs in the game, not while the map is generated.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The XS file, looked up next to the script and then in the game’s XS folder.

details: The file must exist. Map generation, and so the preview, never runs its code.

terms.name: if
terms.summary: Runs the lines that follow only when the label is defined.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Defined by `#define` or `#const`, by the game, or by the run settings.

details: Only whether the label exists counts, not its value: a label defined as 0 holds. The run settings define labels such as the map size (`MEDIUM_MAP`), the game mode (`RANDOM_MAP`), and the player count (`4_PLAYER_GAME`).
Close the block with `endif`; `elseif` and `else` add alternatives, and only the first branch that holds runs. Blocks nest. An `if` inside a random branch that does not run is not evaluated.

terms.name: elseif
terms.summary: Starts a branch that runs when no earlier branch of the `if` ran and its label is defined.

terms.name: else
terms.summary: Starts the branch that runs when no earlier branch of the `if` ran.

terms.name: endif
terms.summary: Ends an `if` block.
details: An `endif` without an open `if` is ignored; an `if` left open ends with the script.

terms.name: start_random
terms.summary: Starts a random block: one roll from 0 to 99 chooses at most one of its `percent_chance` branches.
details: The weights add up in order, and the first branch whose running total reaches the roll runs. If the weights add up to less than 100, sometimes no branch runs; branches after the total passes 100 never run.

Lines in the branches that do not run are skipped, but random values inside them (`rnd`, nested random blocks) are still drawn, so editing a skipped branch can change later results. Close the block with `end_random`; random blocks and `if` blocks can be nested in each other.

terms.name: percent_chance
terms.summary: Starts a branch of a random block, with its weight out of 100.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: The branch’s share of the roll, rounded to a whole number.

details: The first branch also runs on a roll of 0, so it has one extra chance in a hundred. A negative weight is never chosen. Outside a random block the line is ignored, although its value is still worked out.

evidence.note: The extra chance of the first branch follows from the parser’s comparison; no dedicated test.

terms.name: end_random
terms.summary: Ends a random block.
details: A `start_random` without `end_random` is an error; an `end_random` without a block is ignored.

terms.summary: Opens the block of attributes that belongs to the command before it.
details: Braces are words of their own: put spaces or line breaks around them. Blocks do not nest; the game only tracks whether it is inside braces, so a second `{` changes nothing and the first `}` ends the block.

terms.summary: Closes a block of attributes.
details: A `}` outside a block changes nothing.

terms.summary: Starts a comment; everything up to the matching `*/` is ignored.
details: Write `/*` and `*/` as words of their own, with spaces around them. Comments nest. Includes inside a comment are skipped, but `rnd` values inside one are still drawn. A comment left open ends with its file.

terms.summary: Ends a comment started with `/*`.
details: A `*/` outside a comment is ignored.

terms.name: rnd
terms.summary: A random whole number from the minimum to the maximum, both included.

parameters.name: minimum
parameters.description: The lowest result, written as a whole number.

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.description: The highest result, written as a whole number; not below the minimum.

details: Write it as one word without spaces, such as `rnd(3,7)`; the bounds must be plain numbers, not names. It works wherever a number is expected, including `#const` and `percent_chance`.
Every use draws one random number, even `rnd(4,4)`, so adding or removing one changes every random result after it. Put it in a `#const` to reuse one result.

terms.name: random_placement
terms.summary: Places the players around the map in an order the game chooses.

usages.summary: Places the players around the map in an order the game chooses.

details: This is the default. Players stand on a circle when a land block sets `circle_radius`, otherwise along a rectangle around the map. The lobby’s team setting still applies: with teams kept together, teammates end up next to each other.

terms.name: grouped_by_team
terms.summary: Places teammates next to each other, with a gap between teams.

usages.summary: Places teammates next to each other, with a gap between teams.

details: It takes effect when the lobby keeps teams together or fixes positions; with random lobby positions the order stays random. Teammates are spaced by their lands’ `base_size`.

terms.name: direct_placement
terms.summary: Starts each player land at its own `land_position` instead of placing players around the map.

usages.summary: Starts each player land at its own `land_position` instead of placing players around the map.

details: Give each player a `create_land` with `assign_to_player` (or `assign_to`) and `land_position`. Positions inside `create_player_lands` are ignored, so those lands get random positions. `circle_radius` has no effect.

terms.name: nomad_resources
terms.summary: Gives each player the resources for a town center, for starts without one.

usages.summary: Gives each player the resources for a town center, for starts without one.

details: It changes nothing on the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine records the flag; no generation stage reads it.

terms.name: force_nomad_treaty
terms.summary: Keeps players from attacking each other early in a nomad start.

usages.summary: Keeps players from attacking each other early in a nomad start.

details: It changes nothing on the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine records the flag; no generation stage reads it.

terms.name: min_distance
terms.summary: Recognized in `<PLAYER_SETUP>`, but it has no effect.
details: It takes no value: a number after it is read as a separate word and ignored.

evidence.note: Listed in the command table; nothing reads it, and community documentation calls it non-functional.

terms.name: max_distance
terms.summary: Recognized in `<PLAYER_SETUP>`, but it has no effect.
details: It takes no value: a number after it is read as a separate word and ignored.

evidence.note: Listed in the command table; nothing reads it, and community documentation calls it non-functional.

terms.name: set_position
terms.summary: Recognized in `<PLAYER_SETUP>`, but it has no effect.
details: It takes no value. To start player lands at chosen spots, use `direct_placement` with `land_position`.

evidence.note: Listed in the command table; nothing reads it, and community documentation calls it non-functional.

terms.name: behavior_version
terms.summary: Opts the script into later corrections of the generation rules.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The set of corrections to use; 0 keeps the original rules.

details: With 1 or more, the square a land starts with counts toward its `land_percent` or `number_of_tiles`, so lands come out at the size asked for; with 0 the square is usually added on top. It runs in any section; the last one wins.

evidence.note: Our engine models only the land-size correction; community documentation describes further corrections at value 2 that are not modeled.

terms.name: override_map_size
terms.summary: Makes the map a square with the given side length, in tiles.
details: It runs in any section, the last one wins, and every stage uses the new size.

terms.name: set_gaia_civilization
terms.summary: Sets the civilization of Gaia (neutral) objects, which picks their civilization-specific variants.
details: It runs in any section. The last one in the script decides which object variants Gaia gets; in `<OBJECTS_GENERATION>` it can also change the look of Gaia objects.

terms.name: ai_info_map_type
terms.summary: Tells computer players what kind of map this is, so that their strategy fits it.

parameters.name: map_type
parameters.description: A built-in map type name, such as `ARABIA`.

parameters.name: nomad
parameters.description: Marks a start without town centers when 1.

parameters.name: michi
parameters.description: Marks a map whose players are separated by forest when 1.

parameters.name: show_type
parameters.description: Shows the map type in game when 1.

details: It runs in any section and does not change the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine reads nothing from it; operand meanings come from community documentation.

terms.name: effect_amount
terms.summary: Changes an attribute of an object type, or a player resource, when the game starts, as a technology would.

parameters.name: effect
parameters.description: What to do: `SET_ATTRIBUTE`, `ADD_ATTRIBUTE`, `MUL_ATTRIBUTE`, and the other effect names; the `GAIA_…` forms change only Gaia.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: The object type, or a class (`…_CLASS`) for every object of that class.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: An `ATTR_…` attribute, or an `AMOUNT_…` resource for resource effects.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The amount, which may have decimals.

details: Effects run in script order before the map is generated, from any section. Attributes that matter for generation reach the preview: footprint size, movement speed, stored resource amounts, hit points, foundation terrain, standing graphic, and the terrain an object may stand on. Resource effects reach the preview where generation reads the resource: the starting villagers, the starting scout, and the objects some farm types add around their edge when they are completed. Technology effects do not change the map.
The effect, object and attribute must be names: when one of them is a plain number the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`. The value is a plain number.

terms.name: effect_percent
terms.summary: Works like `effect_amount`, but the value is given in hundredths.

terms.name: guard_state
terms.summary: Ties a player rule to an object type: defeat without it, a resource trickle from it, or both.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: The object type the rule watches.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The resource that trickles, an `AMOUNT_…` name.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Sum of 1 (a player without the object loses), 2 (the resource trickles in), and 4 (inverts the condition).

details: It does not change the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine reads nothing from it; operand meanings come from community documentation.

terms.name: water_definition
terms.summary: Chooses how water looks: its color and surface.
details: It does not change the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine reads nothing from it.

terms.name: color_correction
terms.summary: Chooses the color grading of the map, such as a darker or warmer mood.
details: It does not change the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine reads nothing from it.

terms.name: enable_waves
terms.summary: Turns shore waves on (1) or off (0).

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: 1 shows waves along shores, 0 hides them.

details: It does not change the generated map.

evidence.note: The engine reads nothing from it.

terms.name: create_player_lands
terms.summary: Creates one land for every player, each grown from that player’s start position.

usages.summary: Creates one land for every player, each grown from that player’s start position.

details: The attributes in its block apply to every player land. A `land_percent` is shared out between the players, while `number_of_tiles` applies to each land. `land_position` is ignored here. Each player land is in a zone of its own unless a zone command says otherwise.

terms.name: create_land
terms.summary: Creates one land, grown from its `land_position` (or a random spot), or from a player’s position when assigned to one.

usages.summary: Creates one land, grown from its `land_position` (or a random spot), or from a player’s position when assigned to one.

details: Without `assign_to_player` or `assign_to` the land is neutral. Neutral lands without a `zone` share one zone, so they may grow into each other.

terms.name: terrain_type
terms.summary: The terrain the land paints.

parameters.name: terrain
parameters.description: A terrain name. A plain number does not work here: the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`.

usages.summary: The terrain the land paints.

terms.default: `GRASS` (terrain 0); a land does not take the section’s `base_terrain`.

terms.name: base_size
terms.summary: The radius of the square the land starts with, around its origin.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: In tiles; the square is 2 × radius + 1 tiles wide.

usages.summary: The radius of the square the land starts with, around its origin.

details: The base is painted before the lands grow, in script order, so a later land’s base covers an earlier one. It also keeps players and randomly placed lands apart, and keeps player positions away from the map edge.

terms.name: left_border
terms.summary: Keeps the land back from the left edge of the map, in percent of the map width.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Distance from the edge; decimals are allowed.

usages.summary: Keeps the land back from the left edge of the map, in percent of the map width.

details: `border_fuzziness` decides how strictly growth respects the border. The borders also limit where a randomly placed land starts and where players are placed.

terms.name: right_border
terms.summary: Keeps the land back from the right edge of the map, in percent of the map width.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Distance from the edge; decimals are allowed.

usages.summary: Keeps the land back from the right edge of the map, in percent of the map width.

details: `border_fuzziness` decides how strictly growth respects the border.

terms.name: top_border
terms.summary: Keeps the land back from the top edge of the map, in percent of the map height.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Distance from the edge; decimals are allowed.

usages.summary: Keeps the land back from the top edge of the map, in percent of the map height.

details: `border_fuzziness` decides how strictly growth respects the border.

terms.name: bottom_border
terms.summary: Keeps the land back from the bottom edge of the map, in percent of the map height.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Distance from the edge; decimals are allowed.

usages.summary: Keeps the land back from the bottom edge of the map, in percent of the map height.

details: `border_fuzziness` decides how strictly growth respects the border.

terms.name: border_fuzziness
terms.summary: How strictly the land respects its borders while it grows.

parameters.name: chance
parameters.description: Percent chance, per tile of distance beyond a border, that a tile is refused.

usages.summary: How strictly the land respects its borders while it grows.

details: It only applies together with a border (`left_border`, `right_border`, `top_border`, or `bottom_border`). A tile one step past a border is refused with this chance, two steps with twice the chance, and so on; 100 or more refuses every tile past the border. 0 turns the check off, so the borders no longer limit growth. A `land_conformity` above 0 also turns it off.

evidence.note: A community guide says negative values make borders absolute; our engine never refuses a tile then.

terms.name: zone
terms.summary: Puts the land in a zone: lands of one zone may grow into each other, lands of other zones keep apart.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: Any whole number; lands with the same number share a zone.

usages.summary: Puts the land in a zone: lands of one zone may grow into each other, lands of other zones keep apart.

details: Without a zone command each player land has a zone of its own and every `create_land` shares one common zone; writing `zone 0` is not the same as leaving it out. `zone`, `set_zone_by_team`, and `set_zone_randomly` replace each other. `other_zone_avoidance_distance` sets how far apart different zones stay.

terms.name: set_zone_by_team
terms.summary: Puts each player’s land in a zone shared with teammates, so a team’s lands can merge.

usages.summary: Puts each player’s land in a zone shared with teammates, so a team’s lands can merge.

details: A player without a team keeps a zone of its own. A land that belongs to no player gets player 1’s zone.

terms.name: set_zone_randomly
terms.summary: Puts each land of this command in a randomly chosen zone, so some lands may share one.

usages.summary: Puts each land of this command in a randomly chosen zone, so some lands may share one.

details: The zones are chosen from as many as there are players, with one random draw per land.

terms.name: other_zone_avoidance_distance
terms.summary: Keeps the land at least this many tiles away from lands of other zones while it grows.

usages.summary: Keeps the land at least this many tiles away from lands of other zones while it grows.

details: It also spaces randomly placed lands apart when `min_placement_distance` is not set.

terms.name: min_placement_distance
terms.summary: The least distance from other lands when this land’s start is chosen at random.

usages.summary: The least distance from other lands when this land’s start is chosen at random.

details: It only matters for lands without a fixed position: a neutral land without `land_position`, or a player land under `direct_placement` without one. When no spot fits after many tries, the land starts at the map center.
terms.default: A spacing worked out from both lands’ `base_size` and `other_zone_avoidance_distance`.

terms.name: set_circular_base
terms.summary: Makes the land start from a circle instead of a square.

usages.summary: Makes the land start from a circle instead of a square.

details: The radius is `base_size`. Growth around the base is not limited by it.

terms.name: land_conformity
terms.summary: How strongly the land keeps a compact square (or round) shape around its origin.

usages.summary: How strongly the land keeps a compact square (or round) shape around its origin.

details: Each candidate tile outside the shape is refused with this chance. 100 or more paints the shape directly instead of growing it. Any value above 0 turns off the border check of `border_fuzziness`.

evidence.note: A community guide calls it unreliable and says 0 equals leaving it out; our engine still checks the shape on about 1 % of tiles at 0.

terms.name: generate_mode
terms.summary: How a randomly placed land picks its start: 1 allows any spot inside its borders, 0 avoids the corners.

usages.summary: How a randomly placed land picks its start: 1 allows any spot inside its borders, 0 avoids the corners.
Has no effect inside `create_terrain`.

terms.name: land_position
terms.summary: Where the land starts, in percent of the map width (x) and height (y).

usages.summary: Where the land starts, in percent of the map width (x) and height (y).
Has no effect inside `create_player_lands`; player lands start at the player positions.

details: A land assigned to a player only uses it under `direct_placement`. 100 lies one tile past the edge; the preview refuses objects aimed at a land there.

terms.name: assign_to_player
terms.summary: Gives the land to the player in this lobby slot; the land then grows from that player’s position.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Lobby slot 1 to 8; 0 leaves the land neutral.

usages.summary: Gives the land to the player in this lobby slot; the land then grows from that player’s position.

details: If the slot is not in the game, the land and the rest of its block are dropped. It resets `land_id`, so write `land_id` after it. Assigned lands receive `set_place_for_every_player` objects.

terms.name: assign_to
terms.summary: Gives the land to a player chosen by player number, team or color.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: `AT_PLAYER` (by player number), `AT_TEAM` (by team) or `AT_COLOR` (by player color).

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The player, team or color number (colors 1 blue to 8 orange); 0 accepts any player or team, and with `AT_TEAM` a negative number means any team except that one.

parameters.name: pick_first
parameters.description: 0 picks a random eligible player, any other value the first one.

parameters.name: reuse
parameters.description: 1 also allows players who already got a land, 2 does not count this land as used, 0 allows only unused players.

usages.summary: Gives the land to a player chosen by player number, team or color.

details: Teams are counted in lobby order; a team needs at least two players, and other players count as team 0. With `AT_COLOR` the first player in lobby order with that color gets the land, never a random one. When no player fits, the land is dropped. It resets `land_id`, so write `land_id` after it.

evidence.note: The player-number range follows the engine (0 to the player count); not checked against the game.

terms.name: circle_radius
terms.summary: Places the players on a circle around the map center instead of along a rectangle.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: In percent of the map width.

parameters.name: variance
parameters.description: Random offset in tiles on each axis.

usages.summary: Places the players on a circle around the map center instead of along a rectangle; in any land, also one without a player, it moves every player’s land.
Places the players on a circle around the map center instead of along a rectangle.

details: It only counts inside a land block, but it applies to all players’ lands, whichever land block it is written in; the last one wins. It has no effect with `direct_placement` or without player lands.

terms.name: base_terrain
terms.summary: A terrain to fill the map with, or to build on, depending on where it is used.

parameters.name: terrain
parameters.description: A terrain name. A plain number does not work here: the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`.

usages.summary: Fills the whole map with this terrain before the lands grow.
details: The last one outside blocks wins, and it clears an earlier `base_layer`. Lands do not take it over: a land paints its own `terrain_type`. Inside a land block it has no effect.

usages.summary: Places the new terrain only on tiles that have this terrain now.
details: Without `base_terrain` and `base_layer` the terrain goes only on `GRASS` (terrain 0). With `base_layer` but no `base_terrain`, any terrain under the layer qualifies.

usages.summary: Raises hills only on tiles with this terrain.
details: Elevation runs before `<TERRAIN_GENERATION>`, so this is the terrain the lands painted.

terms.name: base_layer
terms.summary: A terrain layer to lay under the map, or to require, depending on where it is used.

parameters.name: terrain
parameters.description: A terrain name. A plain number does not work here: the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`.

usages.summary: Gives every tile this terrain as its layer before the lands grow; tiles a land paints lose it.
details: Write it after `base_terrain`, which clears it. Later `base_layer` filters and `layer_to_place_on` read the layer.

usages.summary: Places the new terrain only on tiles whose layer is this terrain.
details: Without `base_terrain` as well, the terrain under the layer does not matter.

usages.summary: Raises hills only on tiles whose layer is this terrain.
details: When the land section set a `base_layer`, unpainted tiles carry it, so elevation needs the same `base_layer` to build there.

terms.default: No layer: only tiles without a layer qualify.

terms.name: number_of_tiles

terms.name: number_of_clumps

How compact the terrain grows: higher values favour tiles next to the clump.

terms.name: base_elevation
terms.summary: The height of a land’s tiles.

usages.summary: The height of the land’s tiles.

terms.name: land_id

terms.name: set_scale_by_size

terms.name: set_avoid_player_start_areas

terms.name: height_limits

terms.name: create_elevation

usages.summary: Raises hills up to the given height, one level at a time, each grown on the level below.

details: Each level starts from `number_of_clumps` seeds on tiles at the level below and grows to `number_of_tiles`. Hills keep clear of the players’ starting areas (about 9 tiles around each player land’s origin). A height of 0 raises nothing.

terms.name: spacing
terms.summary: Keeps each level of a hill at least this many tiles inside the level below it.

usages.summary: Keeps each level of a hill at least this many tiles inside the level below it.

terms.name: enable_balanced_elevation

usages.summary: Lets hill seeds start close to each other, which spreads hills more evenly across the map.

terms.name: cliff_type
terms.summary: Chooses the cliff style.

usages.summary: Chooses the cliff style.

terms.name: min_number_of_cliffs
terms.summary: The fewest cliffs to draw.

usages.summary: The fewest cliffs to draw.

details: The number of cliffs is chosen from this value up to one less than `max_number_of_cliffs`; when both are equal, exactly that many. A minimum above the maximum is an error.

evidence.note: A community guide describes the maximum as inclusive for lengths; our engine excludes it for both count and length.

terms.name: max_number_of_cliffs
terms.summary: One more than the most cliffs to draw.

usages.summary: One more than the most cliffs to draw.

terms.name: max_length_of_cliff
terms.summary: One more than the longest cliff, in steps of 3 tiles.

usages.summary: One more than the longest cliff, in steps of 3 tiles.

terms.name: cliff_curliness
terms.summary: The chance, in percent, that a cliff turns at each step.

usages.summary: The chance, in percent, that a cliff turns at each step.

terms.summary: The gap kept between cliffs, in steps of 3 tiles.

usages.summary: The gap kept between cliffs, in steps of 3 tiles.

usages.summary: Keeps cliffs away from water and other terrain they cannot cross, in steps of 3 tiles.

terms.name: create_terrain
terms.summary: Paints one terrain over the map in clumps.

usages.summary: Paints one terrain over the map in clumps.

terms.name: percent_of_land
terms.summary: Recognized, but it has no effect; use `land_percent` for a terrain’s share of the map.

terms.name: spacing_to_specific_terrain

parameters.name: terrain
parameters.description: The terrain to keep away from.

usages.summary: Keeps the terrain at least this many tiles away from one other terrain; repeat it for several.

terms.name: terrain_mask
terms.summary: Paints the terrain as a layer instead of replacing the terrain below.

usages.summary: Paints the terrain as a layer instead of replacing the terrain below.

details: 1 keeps each tile’s terrain and records the new terrain as its layer; without `base_layer` only tiles without a layer qualify. 2 paints the new terrain and keeps the old one as the layer. 0 paints normally and clears the layer.

terms.name: beach_terrain
terms.summary: The terrain used for this terrain’s shores where it meets water.

usages.summary: The terrain used for this terrain’s shores where it meets water.

terms.name: create_connect_teams_lands
terms.summary: Connects the lands of teammates with each other; different teams stay unconnected.

terms.name: create_connect_all_lands
terms.summary: Connects every land with every other land, player and neutral alike.

usages.summary: Connects every land with every other land, player and neutral alike.

details: Paths run between the lands’ origins, avoiding terrain whose `terrain_cost` is 0, and paint what `replace_terrain` and `default_terrain_replacement` say; without either, nothing is painted.

terms.name: create_connect_same_land_zones
terms.summary: Connects lands; it works the same as `create_connect_all_lands`.

usages.summary: Connects lands; it works the same as `create_connect_all_lands`.

details: Paths run between the lands’ origins, avoiding terrain whose `terrain_cost` is 0, and paint what `replace_terrain` and `default_terrain_replacement` say; without either, nothing is painted.

terms.name: create_connect_land_zones
terms.summary: Connects all lands of two zones, including the lands within each zone.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: The first zone, as written with `zone`.

usages.summary: Connects all lands of two zones, including the lands within each zone.

details: Paths run between the lands’ origins, avoiding terrain whose `terrain_cost` is 0, and paint what `replace_terrain` and `default_terrain_replacement` say; without either, nothing is painted.
A `create_land` without a `zone` is in zone -10; a player land without one is in its lobby slot number minus 10.

evidence.note: The zone numbers of lands without `zone` are derived from the engine’s storage; no test covers them.

terms.name: create_connect_to_nonplayer_land
terms.summary: Connects each player land to the neutral lands, but not players to each other.

usages.summary: Connects each player land to the neutral lands, but not players to each other.

details: Paths run between the lands’ origins, avoiding terrain whose `terrain_cost` is 0, and paint what `replace_terrain` and `default_terrain_replacement` say; without either, nothing is painted.
Write it after the other connection commands: it can replace connection commands that follow it.

terms.name: default_terrain_replacement
terms.summary: The terrain painted along the paths, for every terrain they cross.

usages.summary: The terrain painted along the paths, for every terrain they cross.

details: It replaces every earlier `replace_terrain` in the block; a later `replace_terrain` still overrides it for its terrain.

terms.name: replace_terrain
terms.summary: Where a path crosses one terrain, paints another.

usages.summary: Where a path crosses one terrain, paints another.

details: Repeat it for several terrains; for the same terrain the last one wins.

terms.name: terrain_cost
terms.summary: What it costs a path to cross one terrain; 0 makes the terrain impassable.

parameters.name: cost
parameters.description: Decimals are allowed; 0 or less blocks the path.

usages.summary: What it costs a path to cross one terrain; 0 makes the terrain impassable.

details: Paths prefer cheap terrain. Repeat it for several terrains.

parameters.description: Tiles painted on each side of the path.

parameters.description: Random change of the size, drawn for every path tile.

details: Size 0 paints the path tile only. A variance larger than the size can leave gaps.

terms.name: accumulate_connections
terms.summary: Makes each connection command build on the paths painted by the ones before it.

usages.summary: Makes each connection command build on the paths painted by the ones before it.

terms.name: create_object
terms.summary: Places objects of one type: a unit, building, resource, or decoration.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: An object name, or the name of an object group. A plain number does not work here: the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`.

usages.summary: Places objects of one type: a unit, building, resource, or decoration.

details: Without attributes it places one Gaia object anywhere on the map. Its block sets how many, how they group, whose they are, and where they may go; `set_place_for_every_player` places them around every player.
With an object group’s name, each object is drawn from the group (see `add_object`). Objects are placed in script order, so earlier commands get the first choice of space.

terms.name: create_object_group
terms.summary: Names a group of object types that `create_object` and `second_object` can place; `add_object` fills it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The group’s name, written directly (not a constant).

usages.summary: Names a group of object types that `create_object` and `second_object` can place; `add_object` fills it.

details: Naming a group again adds to it; `create_object` commands written before that keep the entries they saw. A `#const` or `#define` of the same name takes precedence over the group.

terms.name: add_object
terms.summary: Adds an object type, with a weight, to an object group.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: An object name. A plain number does not work here: the game ignores the whole command, so give the number a name with `#const`.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: A whole number, compared with the roll.

usages.summary: Adds an object type, with a weight, to an object group.
Has no effect inside `create_object`; write it in a `create_object_group` block.

details: Each object placed from the group rolls a number from 0 to 99. The entries whose weight passes the roll qualify, and the roll picks one of them in the order they were written; when none qualifies, the first entry is used. Outside a group block it has no effect.

profileNotes.text: An entry qualifies when its weight is at most the roll: weight 0 always qualifies, and 100 or more never does (such an entry is only used as the first entry when nothing qualifies).
An entry qualifies when its weight is at least the roll: 99 or more always qualifies, and weight 0 only on a roll of 0.

terms.name: create_actor_area

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Half the side of the square, in tiles; negative covers nothing.

terms.name: number_of_objects

usages.summary: How many groups to place; it turns on loose grouping unless tight grouping is set.

parameters.name: count

terms.summary: Varies the size of each group by up to this many objects.

usages.summary: Varies the size of each group by up to this many objects.

details: A group gets from `number_of_objects` minus the variance up to `number_of_objects` plus the variance minus 1 objects, and at least 1, drawn again for every group. It only applies with grouping.

usages.summary: How far the objects of a group may spread from its center, in tiles.

It takes precedence over `find_closest_to_map_center` and `find_closest_to_map_edge`.

terms.name: find_closest_to_map_center
terms.summary: Takes the spots closest to the map center first; with 1, the farthest first.

usages.summary: Takes the spots closest to the map center first; with 1, the farthest first.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`.

terms.name: find_closest_to_map_edge
terms.summary: Takes the spots closest to the map edge first; with 1, the farthest first.

usages.summary: Takes the spots closest to the map edge first; with 1, the farthest first.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`.

terms.name: enable_tile_shuffling
terms.summary: Shuffles spots at the same distance when a `find_closest` command orders them.

usages.summary: Shuffles spots at the same distance when a `find_closest` command orders them.

terms.name: require_path
terms.summary: Uses only spots that can be reached from the player’s land, by a path at most this many tiles longer than the straight line.

usages.summary: Uses only spots that can be reached from the player’s land, by a path at most this many tiles longer than the straight line.

parameters.name: detour
parameters.description: Extra tiles allowed; 0 or no value only asks for some path.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`.

terms.name: force_placement
terms.summary: Places the remaining objects even when no spot meets every rule; only the object’s own terrain needs still count.

usages.summary: Places the remaining objects even when no spot meets every rule; only the object’s own terrain needs still count.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`. Each forced placement places one object, without its group.

terms.name: min_connected_tiles
terms.summary: Places a group only where at least this many connected spots are free.

usages.summary: Places a group only where at least this many connected spots are free.

parameters.name: tiles
parameters.description: A whole number; 1 or less turns it off.

details: It only applies with grouping.

terms.name: avoid_other_land_zones
terms.summary: Keeps the objects inside the zone of the player’s land.

usages.summary: Keeps the objects inside the zone of the player’s land.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Also keeps this many tiles from other zones.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`.

terms.name: actor_area
terms.summary: Marks the area around each placed object with this number, for later `avoid_actor_area` and `actor_area_to_place_in` rules.

usages.summary: Marks the area around each placed object with this number, for later `avoid_actor_area` and `actor_area_to_place_in` rules.

details: The area is a square of `actor_area_radius` around each object.

terms.name: actor_area_radius
terms.summary: The radius of the areas `actor_area` marks, in tiles.

usages.summary: The radius of the areas `actor_area` marks, in tiles.

terms.name: actor_area_to_place_in
terms.summary: Places the objects only inside areas marked with this number.

usages.summary: Places the objects only inside areas marked with this number.

details: With per-player placement, only areas of the same player (or of no player) count. Without such an area nothing is placed.

terms.name: avoid_actor_area
terms.summary: Keeps the objects out of areas marked with this number; repeat it for several numbers.

usages.summary: Keeps the objects out of areas marked with this number; repeat it for several numbers.

terms.name: avoid_all_actor_areas
terms.summary: Keeps the objects out of every marked area.

usages.summary: Keeps the objects out of every marked area.

terms.name: override_actor_radius_if_required
terms.summary: When per-land placement runs out of spots, moves the last candidate to the nearest tile where the object fits.

usages.summary: When per-land placement runs out of spots, moves the last candidate to the nearest tile where the object fits.

evidence.note: Our engine ties it only to the exhausted per-land fallback; a community guide links it to actor areas and buildings.

details: It only applies when the objects are placed per land, with `set_place_for_every_player` or `place_on_specific_land_id`.

families.title: Object attributes
families.summary: Object attributes such as hit points, speed, or stored resources, for the third value of `effect_amount` and `effect_percent`.

families.title: Effect types
families.summary: What `effect_amount` and `effect_percent` do: set, add to, or multiply an attribute, change a resource, enable or upgrade objects, and more. The `GAIA_…` forms change only Gaia.

families.title: Player resources
families.summary: Player resources and counters, such as food, gold, or population, for resource effects and `guard_state`.

families.title: Object classes
families.summary: Object classes, for the second value of `effect_amount` and `effect_percent`, which then change every object of the class.

families.title: Color moods
families.summary: Color moods for the map’s lighting, for `color_correction`.

families.title: Water looks
families.summary: Looks for the map’s water, for `water_definition`.

families.title: Assignment targets
families.summary: How `assign_to` picks a player: by player number (`AT_PLAYER`), team (`AT_TEAM`), or color (`AT_COLOR`).

families.title: Map types
details: Classic map type names, such as `ARABIA`, share no prefix and are shown with the other built-in names.

families.title: Objects, terrains, and other built-in names
families.summary: Names the game defines before every script runs. Most stand for an object (a unit, building, resource, or decoration) or a terrain; what a name means depends on where it is used.
details: A script cannot redefine them: the first definition of a name wins, and these come first.

families.title: Run-setting labels
families.summary: Labels the game defines from the lobby settings: map size, game mode, resources, starting age, positions, players, and teams. Test them with `if`.
details: Each label exists only when its setting applies; the run settings decide which ones the preview uses.

members.TINY_MAP: Defined when the map size is Tiny.
members.MAPSIZE_TINY: Defined when the map size is Tiny.
members.SMALL_MAP: Defined when the map size is Small.
members.MAPSIZE_SMALL: Defined when the map size is Small.
members.MEDIUM_MAP: Defined when the map size is Medium.
members.MAPSIZE_MEDIUM: Defined when the map size is Medium.
members.LARGE_MAP: Defined when the map size is Normal.
members.MAPSIZE_NORMAL: Defined when the map size is Normal.
members.HUGE_MAP: Defined when the map size is Large.
members.MAPSIZE_LARGE: Defined when the map size is Large.
members.GIGANTIC_MAP: Defined when the map size is Huge.
members.MAPSIZE_HUGE: Defined when the map size is Huge.
members.LUDIKRIS_MAP: Defined when the map size is Ludicrous.
members.MAPSIZE_LUDICROUS: Defined when the map size is Ludicrous.
members.RANDOM_MAP: Defined in the Random Map game mode.
members.REGICIDE: Defined in Regicide, as the game mode or as a modifier.
members.DEATH_MATCH: Defined in Death Match, and with ultra-high starting resources.
members.KING_OT_HILL: Defined in King of the Hill, as the game mode or as a modifier.
members.TURBO_RANDOM_MAP: Defined in Turbo Random Map, and in Random Map with turbo on.
members.TURBO_MODE: Defined whenever turbo is on, including Turbo Random Map.
members.SUDDEN_DEATH: Defined in Sudden Death, as the game mode or as a modifier.
members.EMPIRE_WARS: Defined in Empire Wars, as the game mode or as a modifier.
members.DARK_AGE_START: Defined when the game starts in the Dark Age, the standard start of most modes.
members.FEUDAL_AGE_START: Defined when the game starts in the Feudal Age, the standard start of Empire Wars.
members.CASTLE_AGE_START: Defined when the game starts in the Castle Age.
members.IMPERIAL_AGE_START: Defined when the game starts in the Imperial Age.
members.POST_IMPERIAL_AGE_START: Defined when the game starts after the Imperial Age, the standard start of Death Match and Battle Royale.
members.FIXED_POSITIONS: Defined when the lobby keeps teams together or fixes positions.
members.TEAM_POSITIONS: Defined when the lobby fixes team positions.
members.AI_PLAYERS: Defined when a computer player takes part.
members.FULL_TECH_TREE: Defined when the full tech tree option is on.
members.ANTIQUITY_MODE: Defined when the antiquity option is on.
members.SOLID_FARMS: Defined when farms are solid rather than walkable.
members.#_PLAYER_GAME: The number of players, such as `4_PLAYER_GAME`.
members.#_TEAM_GAME: The number of teams with at least two players, from `0_TEAM_GAME` to `4_TEAM_GAME`.
members.TEAM#_SIZE#: The size of each team in lobby order, such as `TEAM1_SIZE2`; a player without allies counts as a team of one.
members.PLAYER#_TEAM#: The team of each player slot, such as `PLAYER3_TEAM2`; team 0 means no team.

snippets.label: start_random … end_random
snippets.summary: A random block: the game rolls once and runs the first branch the roll reaches.

snippets.label: if … endif
snippets.summary: A conditional block: the lines run only when the label is defined.

snippets.label: if … else … endif
snippets.summary: A conditional block with an alternative.

snippets.label: create_player_lands { … }
snippets.summary: One land for every player: terrain, combined size, and starting square.

snippets.label: create_land { … }
snippets.summary: One neutral land: terrain, size, and position in percent of the map.

snippets.label: create_elevation … { … }
snippets.summary: Hills: height, base terrain, size of each level, and number of hills.

snippets.label: cliff settings
snippets.summary: The cliff section’s settings: style, number, length, curliness, and spacing.

snippets.label: create_terrain … { … }
snippets.summary: A terrain painted in clumps, away from the players’ starting areas.

snippets.label: create_connect_all_players_land { … }
snippets.summary: Paths between all players: what they paint across one terrain, its cost, and the path width.

snippets.label: create_object … { … } (every player)
snippets.summary: A cluster of Gaia objects near every player, such as gold or berries.

snippets.label: create_object … { … } (scattered)
snippets.summary: Groups of Gaia objects scattered over the map, scaled with its size.

snippets.label: create_object_group … { … }
snippets.summary: A named group of object types with weights, for `create_object` to draw from.
